title: Who bills for whose services
question: Which San Francisco billing numbers are paid for services that someone else is named as giving, beyond what is ordinary for that kind of provider?
finding: The raw federal rows name two providers for each payment: the number that billed and the number named as giving the service. 15 San Francisco billing numbers stand apart from the ordinary pattern for their kind. Far the largest is the City's own: provider number 1417099789 of the City and County was paid $1,344.1 million from 2018 to 2024, $902.4 million of it for services that 41 organizations under other names are named as giving (the largest: University of California San Francisco $204.6 million; Progress Foundation $112.0 million; Felton Institute $70.1 million); $576.2 million of that was for 27 City-funded nonprofits. That is the pattern to expect where a county runs its own mental-health plan and bills for the organizations it contracts with. 11 of the 15 are outside City government and the University of California; 8 of those are there because services are attributed to provider numbers missing from the California registry file. On the other side, 6 organizations in the Bay Area extract are named as giving $100,000 or more of services under three or more unrelated billing names in one year; none of them is registered in San Francisco. Individual practitioners registered in San Francisco appear under one other billing name in 84% of practitioner-years, and 82 of them under four or more in a single year (up to 19); they are counted, not named.
how: Every released row of the federal file whose billing or servicing number is in the project's provider universe was read (1,665,075 rows). Rows with a blank billing number were left out (10,402 rows, $44.2 million); the artefact rows the publisher's file carries under service code 20, with a blank billing number and trillions of dollars, are not in this extract (0 rows). For each San Francisco billing number the money was split by the servicing number on the row; a servicing organization counts as another body when its registered name differs (all City and County numbers are one body, all University of California San Francisco numbers another, and names joined by a numbered owner in the federal enrolment file are one). A row is shown when an individual's number is paid $100,000 or more for services three or more other practitioners are named as giving; when an organization's number is paid $100,000 or more for services given by organizations under another name; or when $500,000 and a quarter of a number's money is attributed to servicing numbers absent from the California registry file. Each row carries the ordinary pattern for the same kind of provider, taken from the State enrollment record (facility, group or individual). Servicing organizations are shown when three or more unrelated billing names, and $100,000, appear in one year.
limits: Who bills for whom: a group practice or clinic bills for its staff, a hospital for its departments, and a county mental-health plan bills for the nonprofits it contracts with, which is why the City’s number heads the list. A laboratory is routinely named under many billers that send it samples. A provider number absent from the California registry file may be registered in another State (telehealth staff, a national laboratory) or have been deactivated since. A registered address is where a provider said it practises, not where care was given, and many practitioners register a home or a second employer. Different names can belong to one legal body. The file withholds every cell under 12 claim lines or 12 patients, so small relationships are missing, and 2024 is preliminary. Individual practitioners who only appear as the person giving a service are counted and never named.
